There is no scientific link between the MMR (measles, mumps, rubella) vaccine and autism.

The 1998 study that claimed such a link was fully retracted in 2010 due to serious methodological flaws, unapproved procedures, and undisclosed conflicts of interest. Its lead author lost his medical license. Since then, extensive research involving millions of children across multiple countries has consistently found no association between the MMR vaccine and autism spectrum disorder.

Major health organizations including the WHO, CDC, NIH, and the American Academy of Pediatrics all affirm that the MMR vaccine is both safe and effective.
